2608.16829.title: CaliBench: Are the Stochastic Dynamics of Video World Models Physically Calibrated?
2608.16829.paper_summary: Video world models approximate the stochastic distribution of physical outcomes through generative sampling, but existing benchmarks score individual generations or compare distributions coarsely over a whole dataset, leaving the fine-grained aleatoric uncertainty of specific phenomena untested. We introduce CaliBench, which scores outcomes in a physically interpretable discrete space - a bin index, a die face, a suit, a colour - rather than a learned feature space such as in FID, so the distance from a known reference distribution is measured directly. We curate outcome spaces whose reference is known in closed form (binomial Galton boards, Bernoulli forks, uniform dice/cards/lottery, a skewed European-roulette colour), enabling an exact calibration test. We decompose performance into two orthogonal axes that a single accuracy metric conflates: scorability, the fraction of generations yielding a scoreable outcome, and calibration, the total variation distance from the reference on that sample. A chi-squared test assesses significance; as calibration is its null hypothesis it can evidence only miscalibration, and at N=32 per cell detects only large deviations. We apply it to nine scenes and six image-to-video models (WAN-2.7, SeeDance-2.0, HappyHorse-1.0, Veo 3.1, Runway Gen-4.5, Cosmos3-Super), 32 generations each. Models consistently concentrate probability mass on a few outcomes rather than reproducing the reference. Most scene-model combinations are significantly miscalibrated, in the extreme collapsing to one outcome, as Veo 3.1 does on dice. On roulette, generations often leave the ball ambiguously placed, giving several models low scorability. Performance varies by scene: no model dominates all nine. We release the protocol and a metric (mean normalised total variation, mnTV) for comparing new models against our results.
2608.16829.paper_summary_zh: 視頻世界模型通過生成抽樣來近似物理結果的隨機分佈，但現有基準評分單個生成或粗略比較整個數據集上的分佈，未能測試特定現象的細粒度隨機不確定性。我們引入了CaliBench，它在一個物理可解釋的離散空間中評分結果——一個箱子索引、一個骰子面、一個花色、一種顏色——而不是像FID那樣的學習特徵空間，因此從已知參考分佈的距離是直接測量的。我們策劃了參考在封閉形式中已知的結果空間（二項式Galton板、伯努利叉、均勻骰子/牌/彩票、一種偏斜的歐洲輪盤顏色），使得能夠進行精確的校準測試。我們將性能分解為兩個正交軸，而單一的準確性指標則將其混淆：可評分性，即產生可評分結果的生成比例，以及校準，即該樣本與參考的總變異距離。卡方檢驗評估顯著性；由於校準是其虛無假設，它只能證明錯誤校準，並且在每個單元N=32時僅檢測到較大的偏差。我們將其應用於九個場景和六個圖像到視頻模型（WAN-2.7、SeeDance-2.0、HappyHorse-1.0、Veo 3.1、Runway Gen-4.5、Cosmos3-Super），每個模型生成32次。模型始終將概率質量集中在幾個結果上，而不是重現參考。大多數場景-模型組合顯著錯誤校準，在極端情況下崩潰到一個結果，正如Veo 3.1在骰子上的表現。在輪盤上，生成結果經常使球的位置模糊不清，導致幾個模型的可評分性低。性能因場景而異：沒有模型在所有九個場景中佔據主導地位。我們發布了該協議和一個指標（均值標準化總變異，mnTV），用於將新模型與我們的結果進行比較。
